content.title: About
content.content: A hamburger bun made from wheat or cracked wheat flour is soft, slightly sweet, and airy. It serves as a convenient base for burgers, holding meat, vegetables, and sauces without falling apart when heated.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally these buns are made with wheat flour, but some recipes incorporate cracked wheat for a denser texture.
In the United States they are commonly sold in packs of 8–12, while in Russia they are found in bakeries and supermarkets.
Sesame‑topped buns are popular, adding extra aroma and crunch.
Buns can be fresh or frozen; frozen buns retain flavor and structure after baking.
Some versions include a small amount of sugar and milk to improve crust color and softness.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The bun provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain or cracked wheat flour is used, the bun supplies fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, and phosphorus are present, contributing to normal body functions.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Traditional recipes are low in fat, making the bun a suitable component of a balanced diet.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat buns contain gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapidly absorbed carbs may raise blood sugar levels, so portion control is advised for diabetics.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes add salt; excessive sodium intake can affect blood pressure.

items.title: Preservatives in commercial versions
items.content: Store‑bought buns may contain additives and preservatives that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the bun horizontally, lightly toast it on a grill or toaster, then add the patty, cheese, vegetables, and sauces. It can also be used for sandwiches, as a base for appetizers, or served alongside soup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep buns in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or sealed container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in an airtight bag – they retain quality for up to 2 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving.
